newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares firm, boosted by VW surge.
newsitem.headline: German shares firm, boosted by VW surge.

text.p: German shares reopened after a one-day break in solid form on Friday, with firm buying interest in carmaker Volkswagen the highlight of an otherwise lacklustre session.
The blue chip DAX index was up 14.54 points, or 0.4 percent, at 3,452.61 in early bourse trade, with VW notching up an advance of more than four percent.
No single factor appeared to be behind the interest in VW but dealers said the dollar's continued strength and technical buy signals were fuelling the gains.
"The big question is why VW is so strong. I've heard it's because of chart technical factors. The volumes look good," said one trader.
"Car shares are simply in vogue at the moment," said another dealer.
The DAX-100 car share index, which tracks auto shares among Germany's top 100 listed companies, was up nearly two percent in early trade, versus an advance of 0.37 percent for the DAX-100 as a whole.

Dealers predicted the DAX would move in a range of 3,450 to 3,470, with trading likely to be subdued due to the absence of many players who have taken Friday off for an extended weekend break after Thursday's May Day holiday.
The resounding victory of Britain's Labour Party in the general election, ending 18 years of Conservative rule, had little impact on shares here.
Economists said that while Labour's approach towards Europe would be less hostile than that of the Conservatives, policy would not change much in the foreseeable future.

The main event of the day should be the release of U.S. April payrolls data at 1230 GMT, after the close of German bourse dealing, and traders said any weakness in the data could push shares prices higher in afternoon electronic trading.
